question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=ln⁡(8x)$, find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Here $f(x)=ln⁡(8x)$ is a function of a function. We use the chain rule.First, we express $g(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=ln⁡u,\,u=8x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot 8 \\  & =\frac{1}{8x}\cdot 8 \\  & =\frac{8}{8x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{8}}{\cancel{8}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$ f=\ln u,\,u=20 - x.$$

Differentiating gives

$$\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1.$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=\frac{1}{u}\cdot(-1) \\ &=\frac{1}{20 - x}\cdot(-1) \\ &=\frac{1}{x - 20}.\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=19$ is

$$m=\left.(\frac{1}{x - 20})\right|_{x=19}=-1.$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(19,0)$ is $m=-1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(0) &=(-1)(x-(19)) \\ y &=19 - x.\end{aligned}$$
